channel.title: Hastings Daily: On this day
channel.description: Local news for Hastings and St Leonards, three times a day.

item.title: On this day, 1867: No 1 Battery raised at St Leonards in 1867
item.description: No 1 Battery at St Leonards was originally designated as the 7th Cinque Ports Artillery Volunteer Corps and was raised on 23 November 1867. The unit formed part of the broader Volunteer Movement that emerged following an invasion scare in 1859. This enthusiasm led to the creation of many part-time units, including coastal artillery corps along the Kent and Sussex coast, which were later brought together to form the 1st Cinque Ports Artillery Volunteers at Dover in September 1862.

item.title: On this day, 1834: Coastguard boat and six crew lost in 1834 rescue attempt
item.description: On 20 November 1834, a Coastguard boat and her six crew were lost whilst attempting to rescue the crew of the collier Good Intent. This tragedy occurred just four years after the French lugger La Constance was driven ashore at Fairlight in 1830, an event that had previously seen two coastguard officers awarded RNIPLS Gold Medals for their rescue efforts in heavy snow and violent seas.

item.title: On this day, 1997: Michael Foster makes his maiden speech in Parliament
item.description: Michael Foster made his maiden speech on 21 November 1997. He had won the Hastings and Rye seat at the 1997 General Election, where he became the second least expected Labour MP in the landslide. In that election, he defeated the new sitting Conservative MP, Jacqui Lait, by 2,560 votes. Foster served as the Member of Parliament for Hastings and Rye from 1997 to 2010. He was a British lawyer and Labour politician who also served in government as a Minister for Equalities from 2009 to 2010. Foster was born in Hastings, Sussex, and attended the local Hastings Secondary School for Boys and the Hastings Grammar School. He later attended the University of Leicester, where he received a Master of Laws degree. He was admitted as a solicitor in 1980 and worked as a partner of Fynmores Solicitors in Bexhill-on-Sea, specialising in employment law, until 1998.

item.title: On this day, 1928: Funerals held for the crew of the Mary Stanford lifeboat
item.description: On Tuesday 20 November 1928, five days after the RNLI lifeboat Mary Stanford capsized and the entire crew of 17 was lost, the town of Rye gathered for the funerals of fifteen of the men, buried in a communal grave.

item.title: On this day, 1910: Royal Cinema de Luxe held its opening night at Pelham Place
item.description: On 19 November 1910, a thousand people turned up at the opening night of the Royal Cinema de Luxe at Pelham Place, the Sussex Express reported.

item.title: On this day, 1886: Hastings-born filmmaker Geoffrey Malins born in 1886
item.description: On this day in 1886, Arthur Herbert Malins was born in Hastings, Sussex. He would later change his name to Geoffrey Herbert Malins and become a British film director, most famous for his camera and editing work on the 1916 war film The Battle of the Somme. This production combined documentary and propaganda, reaching an audience of over 20 million viewers.

item.title: On this day, 1908: Father Eden dies in office at Ticehurst
item.description: Rev. Arthur Eden died in office on 17 November 1908 at St Mary's Church, Ticehurst. He was subsequently buried in the churchyard on 21 November, surrounded by many loving parishioners and friends. The sentiments of those gathered were summarised by lines written about him by parishioner William J. Courthope, who was sometime Professor of Poetry at Oxford.

item.title: On this day, 2010: ASDA Silverhill opens after plan revisions
item.description: On Monday 15 November 2010, the ASDA Superstore in Silverhill officially opened its doors. The development, situated on the former Marshall Tufflex site, included a café, a pharmacy, and a large car park. A petrol station was added to the site later, opening in 2014.

item.title: On this day, 1865: A 70-foot whale stranded at Pevensey goes on sale
item.description: On 15 November 1865, the carcass of a finback whale some 70 feet long was sold by public auction on the shingle at Pevensey, after it washed up at Norman's Bay two days earlier. A coastguard at the Pevensey Sluice Station spotted the dead animal floating in the water on the evening of Monday 13 November, and it came ashore that night.

item.title: On this day, 1948: Charles Kenward, the Icklesham cricketer, dies at Rye
item.description: On this day in 1948, Charles Kenward, an English first-class cricketer, died at Rye, Sussex. Born at Icklesham Manor House in the village of Icklesham, he was the son of Trayton Kenward, a farmer of over 1,000 acres, and his wife Emily Turtle.

item.title: On this day, 1939: A wartime RAF training wing formed at the Eversfield Hotel
item.description: On this day in 1939, No 5 Initial Training Wing of the Royal Air Force was formed at the Eversfield Hotel in Hastings, in No 54 Group.

item.title: On this day, 1964: This day in 1964: Kevin Ball was born in Hastings
item.description: On this day in 1964, Kevin Ball was born in Hastings. He went on to have a professional football career, according to Wikipedia, with his senior career running from 1981 to 2002 across five clubs: Coventry City, Portsmouth, Sunderland, Fulham and Burnley.

item.title: On this day, 1918: The Armistice reaches the East Sussex papers, 1918
item.description: When news of the Armistice reached Britain on 11 November 1918, newspapers in East Sussex reported on the joy and the solemn reflection of the county.

item.title: On this day, 1967: Final engines stabled at West Marina depot
item.description: On this day in 1967, the last engines were serviced and stabled at the St Leonards West Marina motive power depot. This marked the final end to the site's operational life, following its effective closure in June 1958 due to the transition to diesel traction. The depot, originally established by the LB&SCR in 1846, had served the Hastings area for over a century before the shift in technology rendered its steam facilities obsolete.

item.title: On this day, 1883: Electric street lights trial switched on in Hastings
item.description: This week in November 1883, a trial of electric street lights in the town was switched on.

item.title: On this day, 1922: Pilot Field officially opens with QPR match in 1922
item.description: On this day in 1922, the Pilot Field in Hastings was officially opened with a football match between a Hastings representatives team and Queens Park Rangers. This formal ceremony marked the culmination of a period where the ground had already been in use for two years, serving as a vital hub for local sport since its initial development.

item.title: On this day, 1882: Lifeboat man Edward Robus lost in 1882 Medea rescue
item.description: On 4 November 1882, lifeboat man Edward Robus was swept away and drowned after the Winchelsea lifeboat, the Storm Sprite, capsized twice during rescue attempts. The vessel had been launched to aid the steamship Medea of Sunderland, which was in distress. While the Rye lifeboat successfully took 16 crew off the Medea, the Winchelsea boat suffered a catastrophic failure in the water.

item.title: On this day, 1873: Foundation stone laid for Christ Church expansion in 1873
item.description: On 6 November 1873, the feast day of Saint Leonard, Alexander Beresford Hope MP PC laid the foundation stone for a new building on derelict land adjoining the north end of the old Christ Church. This marked the beginning of construction for a much larger church designed by Sir Arthur Blomfield, which would be built between 1873 and 1875 to supersede the original structure.

item.title: On this day, 1834: Royal arrival at Crown House marks new town's success
item.description: On this day in 1834, the Duchess of Kent and the future Queen Victoria arrived in St Leonards-on-Sea to much public acclaim. The reception featured a triumphal arch, a 21-gun salute, public addresses, banquets, and other festivities. They stayed at Crown House, the first building completed in the planned resort, throughout the winter until January 1835.

item.title: On this day, 1896: This week in 1896: first moving pictures shown on St Leonards Pier
item.description: This week in 1896, the first moving pictures to be shown in Hastings and St Leonards were seen on St Leonards Pier, the local record shows.

item.title: On this day, 1940: An air raid damages every house on The Lawn, St Leonards
item.description: On 11 November 1940, an air attack reached The Lawn, a road of semi-detached houses in St Leonards.

item.title: On this day, 1597: A storm swept away the old Hastings harbour
item.description: A storm swept away the town's harbour on this day in 1597. Between 1595 and 1597, a large and expensive harbour, known as the 'pier', was built in front of Hastings Old Town. On 1 November 1597, a storm swept it away.

item.title: On this day, 2006: The last traders left Hastings Pier
item.description: On 31 October 2006, the last traders on Hastings Pier left the boardwalks. The National Piers Society's news archive records that the businesses on the Promenade Extension, which had remained open, left on that day, and the final event was a Hallowe'en party in the Gritti Palace pub. By the end of it, the structure was padlocked and deserted.

item.title: On this day, 1940: The official end of the Battle of Britain, 31 October 1940
item.description: On 31 October 1940, the Battle of Britain officially came to an end. The British recognise the battle's duration as being from 10 July until 31 October 1940, three months and three weeks of fighting that ended in a British victory.

item.title: On this day, 1869: Frederick North, MP for Hastings, dies at 69
item.description: On this day in 1869, Frederick North, the long-serving Liberal MP for Hastings, died, aged 69.

item.title: On this day, 1966: The Queen and Prince Philip visit the Hastings Embroidery on the pier
item.description: On 28 October 1966, Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip visited the Hastings Embroidery in the Triodome on Hastings Pier, as part of their royal visit to the Hastings area in commemoration of the 1066 battle, the Hastings Observer reports.

item.title: On this day, 1891: The opening of St Leonards Pier
item.description: This week in local history: on 28 October 1891, St Leonards held the opening ceremony of its pier.

item.title: On this day, 1858: Frederic Urquhart born in St Leonards
item.description: On 27 October 1858, Frederic Charles Urquhart was born at St Leonards-on-Sea, Hastings, East Sussex. His father served as an officer in the Royal Artillery, while his uncle was a colonel in a cavalry regiment of the British Army. Educated at Bloxham School in Oxfordshire and Felsted School in Essex, Urquhart left school at fourteen to pursue a career at sea. He obtained a second-officer certificate in the merchant navy and served as a midshipman in the Royal Navy before migrating to Queensland in 1875.

item.title: On this day, 1823: New town hall market opens in the High Street
item.description: On 25 October 1823, the new town hall in the High Street opened its ground floor to the market traders, with 14 stalls taking up their positions.

item.title: On this day, 1705: Pulteney backs Court candidate for Speaker in 1705
item.description: On 25 October 1705, John Pulteney voted for the Court candidate for Speaker in the House of Commons. This decision came shortly after the 1705 English general election, in which he was returned again for Hastings. Pulteney was an English lawyer and Whig politician who sat in the English and British House of Commons from 1695 to 1710.

item.title: On this day, 1909: Michael Daunt: British Test Pilot
item.description: Neill Michael Daunt was born in Hastings on 23 October 1909. He became a British test pilot, a role defined by severe accidents he was lucky to survive, including one for which he had no recollection. His early life was marked by loss, with his father, a General Practitioner, dying in 1920 and his eldest brother, Barry, killed in World War One in 1918. Daunt studied engineering at St Catharine's College, Cambridge, where he learned to fly with the Cambridge University Air Squadron.

item.title: On this day, 2011: Burra's work returns to gallery after 25-year absence
item.description: On this day in 2011, the first major museum exhibition of Edward Burra’s work in more than 25 years opened at Pallant House Gallery in Chichester, West Sussex. The show ran until 19 February 2012 and was accompanied by a new monograph on the artist by the curator, Simon Martin.

item.title: On this day, 1944: Hastings' secret evacuation plans revealed
item.description: On Saturday 21 October 1944, the Hastings and St Leonards Observer printed what the town had not been allowed to know during the war: the full story of the secret plans to evacuate the whole borough in the event of a German invasion.
